name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,801

entries.clue: Funny business with spades covered up by GI (6)

indicatorNotes.covered up by: to cover something up is to wrap it, so the GI's name wraps round the other letters

annotation.surface: Some shady dealing with shovels hushed up by an American soldier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Funny business' looks like one phrase meaning mischief, but 'Funny' alone is the definition. GI Joe is the American soldier; his name opens to take the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: jocose describes a person or remark given to joking, which is what funny means here.

entries.clue: Very entertaining (5)

blocks.note: British informal intensifier, as in '___ good'
cheerful and fun, of a party or outing

annotation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it is just high praise; split it and each word is JOLLY. 'Jolly' as 'very' is everyday British speech, as in 'jolly well done'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are British informal: an adverb as in 'jolly good', and an adjective for a cheerful, fun occasion.

entries.clue: All inside have shelter (7)

blocks.note: to have someone is to trick them, to con them

annotation.surface: Everyone indoors has somewhere to shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have' in the sense 'I've been had' means swindle, which is the hardest step here.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun sense: the content of a box or book is the whole of what is inside it, so 'all inside' fits.

entries.clue: Second person died in warehouse — a docker (9)

indicatorNotes.in: things kept in a warehouse sit inside it, so these letters go inside STORE

blocks.note: in Genesis Eve is the second human, after Adam

annotation.surface: A grim report of a dock worker found dead in a warehouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second person' suggests grammar (you), but here it is Eve. STORE opens as ST...ORE to take EVED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the worker who loads and unloads ships.

entries.clue: Beaten with a fine hypothetical question (4-2)

indicatorNotes.Beaten: beaten eggs are whisked into a jumble, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: f = fine, as on pencil leads

annotation.surface: Someone flogged and fined as well, as though the punishment were a sum.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' looks like the definition but is the instruction to rearrange WITH A F.
annotation.definitionFit: The hyphenated noun names a question that begins with those two words, supposing something that has not happened.

entries.clue: Rental contracts showing great detail (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the second sense is written hi-res

blocks.note: British for rentals: a car or boat taken for a fee
short for high-resolution, of screens and images

annotation.surface: Lease agreements with plenty of small print.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one idea about fussy contracts; the second half is actually an image or screen term.
annotation.definitionFit: Two words spelt the same: rentals, and a shortening of high-resolution.

entries.clue: Upset stomach Romeo fills with vegetable fat (7)

indicatorNotes.fills: to fill a container is to go inside it, so R goes inside TUM

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A tummy upset after a greasy meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset stomach' is a stock phrase, but 'Upset' alone is the definition, a noun, and 'stomach' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: a state of great disturbance.

entries.clue: Spread silence by blocking F1 race at the finish (4,5)

indicatorNotes.blocking: something blocking a pipe sits inside it, so SH sits inside FI
indicatorNotes.at the finish: the finish of a word is its last letter, so take the end of 'race'

blocks.note: the digit 1 read as the letter I

annotation.surface: A motor-racing scene where marshals quieten things as the cars cross the line.
annotation.walkthrough: F1 is read as FI, a common trick with the digit 1. 'By' meaning past is the sneaky step.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this savoury paste is one of many things you spread on bread.

entries.clue: Mean alien leaves Earth, perhaps (4)

indicatorNotes.leaves: to leave is to go away, so the alien's letters go away from the planet

blocks.note: Earth is an example of a planet

annotation.surface: A nasty extraterrestrial abandons our world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as an adjective describing the alien but is a verb of intention.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: 'I mean to go' and 'I plan to go' say the same thing about intention.

entries.clue: Daring to gain access with crowbar (10)

blocks.note: to enter is to get in
to prise is to lever open, as with a crowbar

annotation.surface: A burglar's bold move, forcing a way in with a jemmy.
annotation.walkthrough: Daring here is a noun, the quality of boldness, not an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: readiness to take bold action.

entries.clue: Ashes? Try burning sticks (4,7)

blocks.note: matches are sticks struck to burn

annotation.surface: A tip for turning sticks to ashes: set them alight.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the cricket series between England and Australia; the question mark flags an example. The fire imagery hides the cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: the Ashes is one series of these international cricket games.

entries.clue: Pile of wood set on fire, watched from behind chain (8)

indicatorNotes.from behind: reading from behind means starting at the back, so SEEN is read backwards

blocks.clueFragment: Pile of wood set on fire
blocks.note: a pyre is a heap of wood for burning
watched = seen; turned round to NEES

annotation.surface: A bonfire watched from behind a barrier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chain' seems to be a physical barrier in the scene, but it is a mountain chain.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the mountain range between France and Spain.

entries.clue: Small pony manoeuvred around old beagle (6)

indicatorNotes.manoeuvred: to manoeuvre is to move something about, so the letters of PONY are moved about
indicatorNotes.around: to go around something is to enclose it, so the rearranged pony goes round O

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A little horse steered round an elderly dog.
annotation.walkthrough: The beagle is a particular one, from the Peanuts comic strip.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Charlie Brown's dog in the Peanuts strip belongs to that breed.

entries.clue: Ogre's inside a German cave (6)

indicatorNotes.inside: the inside of a word is everything but its first and last letters

blocks.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

annotation.surface: A fairy-tale ogre lurking in a cavern in Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: It reads as 'the ogre is inside', but it is the ogre's inside: its middle letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for a small picturesque cave.

entries.clue: Bat on and on, a thousand overs to get through (9)

blocks.note: O = overs on a cricket scorecard
to use up is to get through

annotation.surface: A cricketer told to keep batting through a thousand overs.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket scene makes 'Bat' a verb; it is the flying animal, under a very old name.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic word for the flying mammal, from Old English.

entries.clue: Love feeding wild animals? Work behind security screen (4,4)

indicatorNotes.feeding: what feeds animals goes in among them, so O joins their letters
indicatorNotes.wild: wild means out of control, so the letters do not keep their order

blocks.note: love = O, a zero score in tennis

annotation.surface: A zookeeper's affection for wild beasts, then a job in a guarded booth.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the painting hangs in the Louvre behind protective glass.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: Leonardo's painting in the Louvre is shown behind bulletproof glass.

entries.clue: Spray lube and rinse off (9)

indicatorNotes.off: food that has gone off has turned bad, so the letters turn into a new order

annotation.surface: Instructions for a mechanic: spray on lubricant, then wash it away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two fodder words, so LUBE and RINSE are mixed together.
annotation.definitionFit: A device named by what it produces: the medical inhaler turns liquid medicine into a fine mist.

entries.clue: Rise, to allow hosts sleep at last (8)

indicatorNotes.hosts: a host takes guests into the house, so GRANT takes DIE inside

annotation.surface: A plea to be allowed a proper night's sleep at last.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sleep at last' is not the final letter of sleep but death, the last sleep.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a slope, the degree to which a road or ground rises.

entries.clue: Day on lake in rowing boat gives great pleasure (7)

indicatorNotes.in: a lake in the boat sits inside it, so L goes inside EIGHT
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so D comes first

blocks.note: an eight is a racing boat with eight rowers

annotation.surface: A day's rowing on a lake is a joy.
annotation.walkthrough: The rowing boat is the crew boat raced at Henley and in the Boat Race, named for its rowers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym for joy.

entries.clue: Bump into muscly entomologist on vacation (6)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: to vacate a place is to empty it, so the word loses everything but its outside letters

annotation.surface: Colliding with a beefy insect expert while on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' sounds like a holiday; it empties the word, keeping only its outside letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to knock or strike repeatedly, as wind hits a ship.

entries.clue: Computer language with secure structure executed (7)

blocks.note: a fort is a fortified building
a program is executed, that is run

annotation.surface: A programming language with a secure architecture that ran.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Executed' leans towards an execution, but it is the computing sense: the program ran.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an early programming language, short for 'formula translation'.

entries.clue: Stubborn person cracks in response to charm (6)

indicatorNotes.cracks: to crack something is to break into it, so MULE breaks into AT

annotation.surface: An obstinate person gives way when charmed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracks' looks like 'gives in' and 'charm' like persuasion; charm is a noun, the lucky object.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small object worn to ward off harm or bring luck.

entries.clue: Breakfast like small child eats (5)

indicatorNotes.eats: what you eat goes inside you, so TOT takes AS inside

blocks.note: a tot is a small child

annotation.surface: A toddler eating his morning meal.
annotation.walkthrough: The breakfast table picture makes 'eats' look literal, but it is the instruction to take letters inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: grilled bread, a standard morning dish.

entries.clue: Laughing, hail king amongst men outside the church (8)

annotation.definitionNote: Laughing is a gerund here, a noun

indicatorNotes.amongst: to be amongst people is to be in the middle of them, so R goes into LAITY

blocks.note: hi is a greeting, a hail
the laity are people who are not clergy

annotation.surface: Laughter as a king is greeted by a crowd outside a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outside the church' does not wrap anything; with 'men' it defines the laity.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun synonym: loud merriment, the state of everyone laughing.

entries.clue: Having had a few hints, unknown? (5)

blocks.note: y is an unknown in algebra

annotation.surface: Someone who got a few clues yet is still in the dark.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having had a few' reads as having had a few hints; it means having had a few drinks.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'had a few' means had a few drinks, leaving one slightly drunk.

entries.clue: Aviators perhaps serenaded young women (10)

blocks.note: to serenade is to sing to

annotation.surface: Pilots crooning to girls.
annotation.walkthrough: Aviators are pilots in the surface, but here they are a style of eyewear.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: aviators are a teardrop style of these shades, first made for pilots.

entries.clue: Bare arse inscribed with record number of sit-ups, say (4)

indicatorNotes.Bare: to bare something is to strip its covering, so ARSE loses its outside letters
indicatorNotes.inscribed with: an inscription is written into a surface, so EP is written into RS

blocks.note: ARSE with its first and last letters removed
an EP is an extended-play record

annotation.surface: A cheeky gym tattoo on a bare backside tallying sit-ups.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bare' is not naked but stripped: ARSE loses its outer letters. Arse is British slang for backside.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: gym slang for repetitions, the count of one exercise done in a row.

entries.clue: Car seat moved back for East European (6)

indicatorNotes.moved: moved letters no longer sit in their original order, so SEAT is rearranged
indicatorNotes.back for: the back of a word is its last letter, so take the end of 'East'

annotation.surface: Adjusting a car seat to suit a passenger from Eastern Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moved back' looks like one instruction about sliding a seat; 'moved' mixes SEAT and 'back for East' is its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A British car term: a car with an extended rear load space, the American station wagon.

entries.clue: Marc like marque? (6)

blocks.note: a French spirit distilled from grape skins left after pressing
marque = a make of car; the suffix -y means 'like'

annotation.walkthrough: Marc and marque sound alike in French, which is the joke. The second definition is whimsical, hence the question mark: something like a brand is brand-y.
annotation.definitionFit: Marc is a spirit distilled from grape pressings; the second definition jokingly reads a make of car plus the suffix -y.
